newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends down with natgas, forecast.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends down with natgas, forecast.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Monday in line with weaker natural gas futures prices and forecasts of milder weather in the U.S. West through early December, industry sources said.
"It's all related to the lower natural gas," said one power futures broker.
January Henry Hub natural gas futures ended down about 25 cents at near $3.25 per million British thermal units.
Temperatures through much of the U.S. West were called to be normal to above normal from December 4 to 8.

January California Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures finished down $1.07 at $24.60 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trade as low as $24.00, while February COB closed down 60 cents at $19.50 after trading at low as $18.95 per MWh.
Remaining COB months finished down between 10 and 60 cents.
January Palo Verde (PV) settled down $1.16 at $24.19 after trade as low as $24.00, while February PV finished down $1.20 at $19.80 per MWh after trade as low as $19.50.
Remaining PV deferreds settled between 10 and 95 cents lower.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 205 COB and 115 PV contracts traded Monday.
